A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANCHOR study. All 17 pages of each version, including Appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena experiments, scaling studies, component ablations, and a human audit of generated trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, scaling studies, ablations, and human-audit outcomes in Sections 3.4 and 5.

M1.justification: The branch-point generation pipeline, task refinement, verification, step filtering, denoising, and training objectives remain identical in Sections 3–4 and Appendix B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena coverage, including Ubuntu-only scaling and augmentation with Windows trajectories. The added mobile-agent citation introduces no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Zero-Shot, Task-Driven, and Human Data comparisons; Table 4 retains Zero-Shot and Task-Driven comparisons. The trajectory-length comparators in Table 2 also remain unchanged. Android Coach is cited only as background.

E3.justification: Evaluation splits, success metrics, backbone models, and training settings are unchanged. Appendix D retains budgets of 1,000 trajectories for OSWorld and 600 for WindowsAgentArena, with the same optimization and training duration.

E4.justification: Both retain the human verification audit, scaling analyses in Figures 2–3, filtering-and-denoising ablation in Table 5, and qualitative comparison in Appendix C and Figure 11.

E5.justification: Section 3.4 retains the same 100-trajectory audit, 87% agreement, and estimated 95% confidence interval of 79.0%–92.2%. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings are identical. For example, ANCHOR with Qwen3-VL-8B remains at 20.56% on OSWorld in Table 3 and 30.76% on WindowsAgentArena in Table 4.

T1.justification: Trajectory and branch-point definitions, filtering notation, and the planning/action loss equations remain unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable branch-point supervision, data quality, benchmark improvements, and cross-platform generalization.

C2.justification: Explanations of scaling behavior, branch-point benefits, and evaluation variability are unchanged. The Limitations section retains the desktop evaluation boundary and proposed extensions to mobile and web settings.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, action schema, seed-task IDs, and annotator information remain identical. The code and data/model link destinations are also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gan et al. (2026), Android Coach, to the introductory examples of mobile GUI agents and adds its bibliography entry. Section 2 and the substantive positioning of ANCHOR remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The textual edits are limited to the added introductory citation and reference entry, plus the updated arXiv version/date header. The narrative and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The citation changes line wrapping on page 1, and the added reference reflows the bibliography across pages 9–10. All figures, tables, and appendix pages retain identical rendered layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly expands background attribution with the Android Coach citation. The method, evidence, explanations, limitations, reproducibility information, and appendices remain unchanged, while the small layout adjustments preserve readability. These edits establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
